cards.text: Baker, welcome back! Joash is king in Jerusalem now, and his mother is Zibiah, from Beersheba. Let's see how this reign goes.

cards.question: Joash reigns in Jerusalem for ___ years.

cards.text: And Joash has a great teacher in his corner: Jehoiada the priest. Every king needs a guy like that, baker. Back in the junk drawer, my wisest advisor was an expired coupon!

cards.question: As long as Jehoiada the priest is instructing him, Joash does what is right in the eyes of the LORD.

cards.text: Then comes a word I can't stand, baker: nevertheless. OOH. That's the 'but' in 'Great batch, Papa, BUT…'

cards.question: Joash does what's right. Nevertheless, what's still a problem in his reign?

answers.text: The high places are not removed
The temple of Baal is rebuilt

cards.text: The people keep sacrificing and burning incense at those high places. Meanwhile, Joash calls in the priests with a plan about money.

cards.question: What money does King Joash tell the priests to collect?

answers.text: All the money brought as sacred gifts
A new tax from every town in Judah
Silver from the priests' own homes

cards.question: Joash names three kinds of sacred gift money: the census money, the money from vows, and the money brought ___.
What is King Joash's sacred gift money supposed to be used for?

answers.text: Making gold articles for the temple

cards.text: Each priest collects from his own constituency, and the money goes to the repairs. Simple plan, baker, and then the years roll by.

cards.question: By the twenty-third year of Joash's reign, the priests have finished repairing the temple.

cards.text: TWENTY-THREE YEARS, baker. I sat in a junk drawer for years, and even I'M saying that's a long wait!

cards.question: King Joash calls in Jehoiada and the other priests. What does he ask them?

answers.text: Why they haven't repaired the temple
Where all the census money went
Who caused the damage to the temple

cards.question: Joash tells the priests to take no more ___ from their constituency, but to hand it over for the ___ of the temple.

cards.text: So the priests agree to the new deal: no more collecting money from the people.

cards.question: Under the new deal, the priests will still repair the temple themselves.

cards.text: So Jehoiada the priest takes a chest and bores a hole in its lid. Baker, that's a tip jar that means BUSINESS.

cards.question: Where does Jehoiada set the chest with the hole in its lid?

cards.text: The priests who guard the threshold drop in all the money brought to the house of the LORD. And whenever that chest fills up, it's counting time.

cards.question: When there's a large amount of money in the chest, who comes up to count it?

answers.text: The royal scribe and the high priest

cards.question: Once the money from the chest is counted, they tie it up in ___.

cards.text: Then the counted money goes into the hands of the men supervising the work on the house of the LORD.

cards.question: Who do the supervisors pay with the money from the chest?
The chest money also buys timber and dressed stone to repair the house of the LORD.

cards.text: Now think about everything a temple could spend money on, baker. Silver basins, sprinkling bowls, trumpets, articles of gold.

cards.question: The chest money is used to make silver basins and trumpets for the house of the LORD.

cards.text: Instead, it all goes to the workers, and with it they repair the house of the LORD. FINALLY!

cards.question: Why is no accounting required from the men who pay the workers?

answers.text: Because the scribe counted it first
Because the king ordered it so

cards.text: No receipts, baker. NONE. The junk drawer I lived in was half receipts, and these guys don't need ONE!
Not every coin goes to the repairs, though. The money from the guilt offerings and sin offerings isn't brought into the house of the LORD.

cards.question: The money from the guilt offerings and sin offerings belongs to the ___.

cards.text: Then trouble shows up. Hazael, king of Aram, marches up, fights against Gath and captures it, and then he decides to attack Jerusalem.

cards.question: With Hazael king of Aram set to attack Jerusalem, what does King Joash do?

answers.text: He sends Hazael the sacred objects
He marches out to fight Hazael
He hides in the house of the LORD

cards.question: Along with the sacred objects from his fathers and his own consecrated items, Joash sends Hazael all the ___ found in the treasuries of the temple and the palace.
After Joash sends him everything, Hazael king of Aram withdraws from Jerusalem.

cards.text: Baker, that's handing over the WHOLE cookie box just to get somebody off your porch. The rest of what Joash did is written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah.

cards.question: Joash's forty years on the throne come to a hard end. How?

answers.text: His servants conspire and kill him
He dies in battle against Hazael
He falls sick in the palace

cards.text: His servants Jozabad son of Shimeath and Jehozabad son of Shomer strike him down at Beth-millo, on the road down to Silla. And Joash dies.

cards.question: Where is King Joash buried?

answers.text: With his fathers in the City of David
In his mother's town of Beersheba

cards.question: After Joash dies, his son ___ reigns in his place.

findings.problem: The opening line "Baker, welcome back!" assumes something about this baker's history, namely that they've been here before. Papa Dorin isn't told how a baker has done before, and every baker gets the same lesson.

rule.text: What he doesn't know: anything about the individual baker that he hasn't been told, such as their streak, their mood, the time of day or how they've done before. In lessons, he's never told, because every baker gets the same lesson.

findings.problem: "Meanwhile, Joash calls in the priests" adds a time relationship the text doesn't give. 2 Kings 12:4 says "Then Joash said", and nothing says it happened at the same time as the worship at the high places.

rule.text: Times stay true. No time in the text means none added.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to guess the exact wording of the third item in Joash's list ("brought voluntarily"). Nothing on the earlier cards lets the baker reason it out. It tests wording they haven't seen, not meaning.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: "TWENTY-THREE YEARS" presents the delay as a 23-year wait. 2 Kings 12:6 only says that by the twenty-third year of Joash's reign the repairs weren't done. The text never says when Joash gave the order, so the length of the wait isn't stated.

rule.text: Times stay true. No time in the text means none added.

findings.problem: Asking what the counted money is tied up in (bags, baskets or cloths) is a minor detail. The baker doesn't need it to understand the passage, and they can only guess it.

rule.text: Ask about the moments that move the passage forward and the details the baker needs to understand it.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "Because the scribe counted it first" is arguable. The royal scribe and the high priest did count the money before handing it over (2 Kings 12:10), so a baker could argue it explains why no accounting was needed.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.
